content: Self-indulgence is justly censured, because it belongs to us not as human beings, but as animals.
author: Aristotle
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

Across his life and work, Aristotle saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
